notes: States 0-4 are replaced by *state-8 ('pre-breach, can safely throw away'): the whole state is dropped and bunted. Treating pre-breach data as worthless is an operational call.

ops: in(associations: map(in(md-resource: in(app-name: convert), in(path: plunge(ship))), in(metadatum: in(module: convert))))
notes: migrate-app-to-graph-store %publish: for %publish entries only, app-name becomes %graph, a 2-element path gets a %ship prefix, and module is set to %publish. Deterministic rekeying.

ops: in(associations: map(in(md-resource: in(app-name: convert), in(path: plunge(ship)), in(path: compute)), in(group: compute), in(metadatum: add(picture), add(preview), add(vip))), filter); remove(group-indices); remove(app-indices); remove(resource-indices)
notes: Same %chat->%graph rekey as 5->6, then associations-1-to-2: group and resource paths are parsed to resource (entries that do not parse are dropped by murn), %contacts becomes %groups, and picture/preview/vip are added (preview=%.n, rest bunt). The cached index jugs are dropped (base-state-2 ends in ~) and rebuilt at the end of on-load. Has filter and cache-discard components.

ops: in(associations: map(in(metadatum: remove(module), add(config: compute), add(hidden), remove(picture), add(picture), remove(vip), add(vip))))
notes: metadatum-2-to-3: module becomes config ([%group ~] when module is empty, otherwise [%graph module]) and hidden=%| is added. It starts from *metadatum and copies only some fields, so picture and vip are silently reset to bunt (a discard side effect).
Tag bump only.

No state change. For each %groups association whose config names a feed hosted by another ship, it pokes graph-pull-hook %add (wire /fix-feed). The intent is repair (re-pulling feeds), and picking which feeds to re-add is an operational judgement.

hide-dm-assoc sets hidden=%& for %graph resources whose name parses as 'dm--<ship>'. It infers meaning from a naming convention (18862efc82 changed it from dropping these to hiding them). Could be coded derive.

reset-group-hidden forces hidden=%| on every %groups association (1c04bdec68 'unhide all groups'). It undoes bad hidden flags with a blanket reset, which is a judgement. The code does not say which bug set them, so repair is inferred.
Inserts refresh-rate=~m5 (a constant) after url in each watchdog config.
Tag bump. Emits a %b %wait timer for every watchdog (0eaad536a0 'keep timers going'). The intent is to restart lost timers.
Inserts eager=| (a constant) into each config.

ops: in(dogs: map(in(config: add(timeout-time: compute)), in(running: map(add(since: compute)))))
notes: timeout-time = 6*refresh-rate is computed from an existing field, and a running thread gets since=now. Could be coded add, since the values are formula defaults.

ops: in(dogs: map(in(config: add(batchers)), in(pending-logs: map(map(in(mined: map(add(input)))))), in(history: map(map(in(mined: map(add(input))))))))
notes: Adds batchers=~ to config. Each event-log's mined gains input=~, done by a noun-level trick (?~(mined ~ `mined) re-reads [~ x] as [~ [~ x]], i.e. input=~ prepended).

ops: in(dogs: map(in(config: add(to)), in(running: map(in(since: compute)))))
notes: Adds to=~ to config. It also resets running.since to now, which is a compute from now and not from state. 0ef9570f06 fixed this step, which had wrongly copied refresh-rate into timeout-time.

Rewinds each dog's block number to the block of the newest mined log in history (7086d8c07d 'rewind last block'), so that blocks possibly skipped get re-fetched. Emits a timer for every dog. Rewinding to the last log is an operational choice.
Adds ship-quota (bunt) and the constants slice=~d7, quota=7, resend-time=~m5, update-rate=~m1. Emits a quota timer (set-quota from now and slice).
Adds spo (sponsors) as an empty map (bunt). The map is not rebuilt from pre.
allowances is a bunt. next-slice is the next whole slice after now, computed from the existing slice field and now. Mostly add.
fallback-gas-price=10.000.000.000 (a constant).
Each raw-tx in sending is paired with force=| (a constant).
Each sending tx gets its signer address, recovered from the raw tx signature with pre and chain-id (extract-address). It falls back to 0x0 when recovery fails.

ops: remove(grams); add(grams); in(known: map(in(target: add(in-group)))); in(bound: map(in(target: add(in-group)))); in(binds: map(map(add(in-group)))); in(audience: map(add(in-group)))
notes: grams (the message cache) is set to ~ ('only impacts historic message lookup'). Every target is wrapped with in-group=| (a constant). Could be coded add.
Drops the sole console state and entropy (moved to shoe).

ops: remove(grams); remove(known); remove(count); add(sessions: compute); in(bound: map(in(target: remove(in-group), in(path: head), rename(path, name)))); in(binds: map(map(remove(in-group), in(path: head), rename(path, name)))); remove(audience)
notes: Moves from chat-store to graph-store. Each target [in-group ship path] becomes resource [ship name], where name is the first path element. A single default session 'drum_~our' is built whose audience is one arbitrary element of the old audience set, and the rest are lost. grams, known and count are dropped. Emits %leave to chat-store and invite-store. Heavy discard component.
Session keys @ta 'drum_~ship' are parsed into sole-id [ship %$] by upgrade-id. Keys that do not parse are dropped (murn). Emits a %kick on every old /sole/<id> subscription.
Adds spo=*sponsors (bunt).

ops: add(refresh); add(sap); in(nas: compute); in(own: compute); in(spo: compute)
notes: Jumps straight to %7 (state-5-to-6 then state-6-to-7 add refresh=~m5 and sap=bunt). nas, own and spo are recomputed by replaying logs from a bunt naive state (run-logs), and the resulting udiffs are sent to Jael.

ops: remove(nas); add(nas); remove(own); add(own); remove(spo); add(spo); remove(logs); add(logs); in(url: convert); add(refresh); add(sap)
notes: As the code now stands, nas/own/spo come from sap after state-6-to-7 has bunted it, so the PKI state is wiped. url is forced to a hard-coded mainnet endpoint, jael-update cards are emitted for the (empty) snapshot, and log retrieval restarts (start:do). In the original 583d5f5063 these fields were replaced from a compiled-in snapshot file ('process snapshot on-load'), which would code derive/reshape with o. The step went stale when sap moved into state.
Tag bump. Emits %j %resend so that Jael re-gives the private key to subscribers (8535563de6). A one-time action.

ops: remove(nas); add(nas); remove(own); add(own); remove(spo); add(spo); remove(logs); add(logs)
notes: Runs the %watch poke handler. On %default it resets nas/own/spo to the snapshot (now the bunted sap) and clears logs, otherwise it bunts them. 0c9fc76b93: state may be incomplete after a reorg bug in zoom-margin, so it 'rewinds the Azimuth state to the contents of the snapshot'. The handler returns no cards. In the current code the effect is a discard.
refresh=~m5 (a constant).
sap=*snap-state (bunt).
%0 and %1 crash (!!) on load. A refusal to load, with no conversion path.

ops: in(graphs: map(in(graph: map(in(post: in(contents: filter)))))); in(archive: same); in(update-logs: map(map(in(add-graph|add-nodes: in(post: in(contents: filter))))))
notes: contents-to-one drops every %reference content, since the reference type changed from uid to a richer $reference and old ones are not converted. This is recursive over nested graphs and over logged %add-graph and %add-nodes.

ops: in(graphs: map(in(graph: map(in(post: wrap(%&)))))); in(archive: same); remove(tag-queries); add(tag-queries); remove(validators); in(update-logs: map(remove; add))
notes: Every post becomes maybe-post [%& post] (a wrap, recursive). tag-queries are bunted (key type changed to uid), validators are removed, and every update-log is wiped to bunt. A substantial discard component.
For each graph whose log is empty (all of them after 3->4), it seeds the log with one logged %add-graph of the whole graph at now. Crashes if a graph has no log entry (got).
For resources hosted by other ships, truncates the update-log to its 2 newest entries (1a2a9ee899 'drop unnecessary logs'). Logs of our own resources are kept. Keeping 2 is an operational choice.

ops: in(graphs: filter, map(in(graph: map(in(post: in(signatures: remove; add)))))); in(update-logs: filter, map(map(in(signatures: remove; add)))); remove(archive); add(archive)
notes: Drops old DM graphs and logs (resource name prefixed 'dm--'), strips all signatures (ce1332565e), and empties archive. Before dropping, archived and old-DM graphs are backed up by pokes to hood drum-put. nuke-groups scries gall (%gu/%gd for %groups) and pokes kiln-nuke and docket-uninstall for groups and %talk. Matching on the name prefix and uninstalling apps are judgements.
